title: Salt and Hollow
premise: Marguerite Villalobos, a mercenary whose god fell silent two decades ago when magic was outlawed in the city of Vell Hollow, survives by selling charms that no longer work. When a mute child named Oren arrives at her door speaking the pre-kingdom tongue of the deep courts, she discovers he carries a stolen soul—her own brother's, sold beneath the mountain before she was born. Hunted by the Inquisitors' Guild and guided by a disgraced archivist and a moon-priestess who remembers everything, Marguerite must descend into the court beneath the mountain to steal the soul back before the thirteenth turn of the moon seals it forever. She succeeds at terrible cost: her god's silence is broken only as she gives up her own memories of him, and the outlawed magic returns to Vell Hollow through the child who carried it home.
about_author: Bram Sterling is the pen name of a former courtroom clerk who spent eleven years transcribing testimony before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people the law forgot, from a house built over an old salt road.

chapters.title: The Charm That Would Not Light
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. On the eve of the moon's twelfth turn, Marguerite sells a dead woman's protection charm that fails in front of the buyer, nearly earning her a Guild whipping. That night, a barefoot boy appears at her door speaking a language older than any kingdom. Emotional beat: weary resignation cracking into dread and wonder.

chapters.title: A Language Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The boy, Oren, cannot speak Common but his words make Marguerite's dormant god-mark burn for the first time in twenty years. An Inquisitor patrols her street; she hides the child in her cellar among unsold charms. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: What the Salt Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Oren. Through the boy's eyes, the city is a wound: he hears the mountain humming, sees souls like moths trapped in lamplight. He knows Marguerite's name before she gives it. Emotional beat: alienation softening as he decides this stranger is his way home.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Debt
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. She seeks out Sefa Ilvane, a disgraced royal archivist living in exile, who translates one phrase of Oren's speech: 'the thirteenth turn closes the door.' Sefa recognizes the dialect of the court beneath the mountain—and recognizes Marguerite's family name on a centuries-old debt ledger. Emotional beat: the past arriving like a bill come due.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Ash
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Sefa reveals the Villalobos line sold a soul to the under-court generations ago to buy their freedom from a blood-feud—the soul was her unborn brother's. Her silent god was the witness who refused to forget. Emotional beat: grief for a sibling she never met becoming purpose.

chapters.title: The Moon-Priestess
chapters.summary: POV Ysolde. Ysolde, last priestess of the outlawed lunar order, has counted the turns from her rooftop shrine. She confirms the deadline and warns that the under-court will demand a price no one expects. She agrees to read the moon-road for them. Emotional beat: lonely vigilance finding kinship.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The company forms: Marguerite, Oren, Sefa, Ysolde. The Guild posts a bounty after a charm-seller informant reports strange tongues in the Hollow district. First skirmish with Inquisitors; they escape through the salt-cellars. Emotional beat: camaraderie forged under threat.

chapters.title: The Road Under the Road
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The archivist leads them into abandoned mine-shafts where old contracts are carved into stone. He confesses he was exiled for copying forbidden ledgers—he has been waiting twenty years for someone with a reason to go down. Emotional beat: guilt transmuted into devotion.

chapters.title: Where the God Went Silent
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. At a shrine deep in the tunnels, Marguerite relives the night her god stopped answering: the day the Edict of Silence passed and every sworn mercenary chose survival over faith. She chose survival. The mark on her wrist aches toward the dark below. Emotional beat: shame confronted, not yet forgiven.

chapters.title: Moths in the Lamplight
chapters.summary: POV Oren. The party passes a village of the half-forgotten—people whose names were sold piecemeal to the under-court. Oren can hear their missing syllables humming in the walls. Ysolde leaves an offering. Emotional beat: horror at what justice-by-contract costs the powerless.

chapters.title: The Tollgate of Names
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. A gatekeeper wraith demands a true name as toll. Sefa offers his own, losing his memory of why he came; they bind him to the group with rope and ritual so he won't wander. Emotional beat: sacrifice made intimate and frighteningly small-seeming until it isn't.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. They reach the under-court: a cathedral of salt where the Thirteenth Magistrate keeps souls in lanterns. Marguerite finds her brother's soul—a small blue flame that flinches from her like a startled bird. Emotional beat: awe curdling into cold resolve.

chapters.title: Terms of Trade
chapters.summary: POV Ysolde. The Magistrate offers a bargain: the brother's soul for Oren, whose body was made to carry souls across thresholds. Ysolde reads the fine print carved in the floor—it's a trap written in the pre-kingdom tongue only Oren can parse. Emotional beat: temptation versus clarity.

chapters.title: What the Child Knew All Along
chapters.summary: POV Oren. Oren reveals he wasn't sent to find help—he was sent as payment, and he knew. He chose Marguerite because her god's mark means she can carry a soul without burning. Betrayal and forgiveness collide. Emotional beat: heartbreak maturing into trust freely given.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Turn Wanes
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. With one turn left, the party plans the theft instead of the trade: swap the brother's flame with a decoy soul bought from the half-forgotten village. Sefa, nameless and drifting, still remembers ledger-craft and draws the vault's wards from memory. Emotional beat: desperate hope organized into a plan.

chapters.title: Lanternfall
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The heist begins. Ysolde douses the great lamps with consecrated dark; Oren sings the wards asleep in the old tongue. They lift the flame—but the decoy soul screams, waking the court. Emotional beat: triumph collapsing mid-breath.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Judgment
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Cornered, Marguerite invokes her old oath, demanding trial by the terms of the original contract: the debt was paid in full generations ago, and the soul was held past term. The Magistrate must convene judgment. Emotional beat: the mercenary finally fighting with law instead of steel—justice outside the law, using its own bones.

chapters.title: Witness
chapters.summary: POV Ysolde. At judgment, the silent god answers at last—not with words but through Marguerite's mark, which blazes as living testimony that the contract expired. The Magistrate, bound by older law than itself, releases the soul. But it demands a vessel's price: the memories of the one who claimed it. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by coming loss.

chapters.title: The Price of the Flame
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. To carry her brother's soul out, Marguerite surrenders her memories of her god—every prayer, every answered blade, twenty years of faith. She walks out of the mountain holding a warm lantern and an empty chest where devotion used to live. Emotional beat: grief and release entwined.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: POV Oren. As the moon completes its turn above ground, the door beneath the mountain grinds shut forever—with the Guild waiting at the tunnel mouth. Oren steps forward and speaks the old tongue aloud, and the returning magic floods Vell Hollow, breaking the Edict of Silence in a single ringing chord. Emotional beat: the smallest voice ending the longest silence.

chapters.title: Salt and Hollow
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Weeks later, magic is legal again and chaotic; charms work, Inquisitors resign in droves. Marguerite doesn't remember her god, but her mark still warms when Oren laughs, and her brother's soul—now a quiet presence in a salt lamp—feels like family. Emotional beat: peace earned, identity rebuilt from what remains.

chapters.title: The Ledger Left Open
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The archivist, nameless but free, opens a new ledger in the rebuilt archive and writes the first entry: debts owed to the half-forgotten, to be repaid by the city that profited. Marguerite takes a commission as the court's first outside advocate. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed—from what we're owed to what we owe.
